selected_primary_idea.title: Beyond Element 118: A Calibrated, Evidence-Aware Frontier for Conditional New-Element Reachability
selected_primary_idea.summary: Use a time-versioned corpus to model nuclear stability, scenario-conditional reachability, and discovery-proof sufficiency separately. Compare calibration against stability-only and technology-only baselines; abstain rather than force an endpoint claim.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Published superheavy-nucleus and discovery-evidence records, not a new nuclear reaction.
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: The three-layer model produces better calibrated historical reachability classifications than prespecified simpler baselines.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Separating physical, technological, and evidentiary components prevents a model score from being mistaken for a discovery or a final periodic-table boundary.
falsification_conditions: D2 does not improve calibration or discrimination over stability-only and technology-only baselines.
Time-split validation exposes unacceptable model-era leakage.
The abstention mechanism cannot identify evidence-insufficient cases reliably.
Expert review finds that the evidence schema cannot represent the relevant discovery logic.
planned_contributions: A four-layer definition of periodic-table completeness.
A versioned corpus and evidence graph for new-element reachability claims.
A claim-language contract that reserves discovery recognition for IUPAC/IUPAP.

rejected_ideas.title: Single-number final atomic number forecast
rejected_ideas.reason: Conflates physical limits, technology, evidence, and recognition; unsupported by the Survey evidence.

mcts_evolution_summary.root_defect: The phrase 'complete periodic table' wrongly collapses several endpoint concepts.
retained_edits: Replace endpoint extrapolation with conditional reachability.
Retain uncertainty and abstention rather than force a prediction.
Encode proof-chain completeness separately from physics plausibility.
mcts_evolution_summary.discarded_edit: Infer a final atomic number directly from the current recognized maximum.
